objects.description: Utility class providing static string and UTF-8 helpers and constants for HTML parsing. It is non-instantiable (private default constructor) and exposes only static members. Includes whitespace/escape character sets and numerous manipulation, encoding/decoding, and comparison routines.

URL parsing and inspection class. Constructs from a URL string_view, parses components (protocol, authority, host, login, port, path/params/fragment) and exposes getters and internal validation helpers. Designed for read-only access to parsed fields after construction.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::DecodePercentEncodedURL
functions.description: Decodes a percent-encoded URL string (e.g., "google.com%20%2F%20%3Fx%3Db" -> "google.com / ?x=b"). Use when you need a decoded representation of a URL or URL component.
requirements: uri may reference external storage; it must remain valid only for the duration of the call.
On invalid percent-encoding, returns std::nullopt; callers must handle the optional result.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::ToHexString
functions.description: Returns a hexadecimal string representation of a 4-byte code point value.
requirements: Input is a 32-bit unsigned value; behavior for values outside Unicode scalar range is not specified (result is still a hex string).

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::IsCharAlphabet
functions.description: Returns true if c is an ASCII alphabet letter (A–Z or a–z).
requirements: c is interpreted as a byte; only ASCII ranges 0x41–0x5A and 0x61–0x7A are considered alphabetic.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::IsDigit
functions.description: Returns true if c is an ASCII digit ('0'–'9').
requirements: c is interpreted as a byte; only ASCII range 0x30–0x39 are considered digits.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::ConvertNewLines
functions.description: In-place converts Windows/Mac newlines to Unix: transforms "\r\n" and "\r" into "\n". The resulting string may shrink.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::CodePointByteSequenceCount
functions.description: Determines the expected UTF-8 sequence length based on the first byte. Returns the number of bytes (2, 3, or 4) for leading bytes, or other value per implementation for invalid/ASCII cases.
requirements: c is a raw byte from a UTF-8 encoded sequence.
Return value semantics for ASCII (single-byte) and invalid leading bytes are per implementation; callers should be prepared for non-2/3/4 values.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::CodePointNumBytes
functions.description: Returns how many bytes are required to UTF-8 encode the given Unicode code point.
requirements: c should represent a Unicode code point; values outside UTF-8 encodable range or surrogate range may yield error-indicating value depending on implementation.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::DecodeUtf8Symbol
functions.description: Decodes the next UTF-8 code point from the beginning of the given string_view, advancing the view past the decoded sequence on success. Returns std::nullopt on invalid UTF-8 or unpaired surrogate in a three-byte sequence.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid std::string_view.
The view referenced by *s must remain valid for the duration of the call and its underlying buffer must outlive the call.
On success, *s is modified to start after the decoded code point; callers must account for the consumed bytes.
Callers must handle std::nullopt for invalid data.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::EncodeUtf8Symbol
functions.description: Encodes a Unicode code point into its UTF-8 byte sequence. Returns std::nullopt on error (e.g., code point not encodable in UTF-8).
requirements: code_point should be a valid Unicode scalar value (up to 21 bits; surrogates are invalid).
Callers must handle std::nullopt.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::Utf8ToCodepoints
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 string into a vector of Unicode code points, stopping at the first invalid sequence.
requirements: utf8 must be valid UTF-8 to obtain a full conversion; invalid data will stop decoding early.
utf8 must remain valid only during the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::AppendCodepointToUtf8String
functions.description: Appends the UTF-8 encoding of the given code point to an existing string. If encoding fails, appends a single space character.
requirements: utf8_str must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.
code should be a valid Unicode scalar value to avoid fallback behavior.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::CodepointToUtf8String
functions.description: Returns a new string containing the UTF-8 encoding of the given code point. Returns an empty string on encoding error.
requirements: code should be a valid Unicode scalar value.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::CodepointsToUtf8String
functions.description: Converts a sequence of Unicode code points to a UTF-8 string; code points that fail to encode are skipped.
requirements: codes elements should be valid Unicode scalar values.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::IndexAny
functions.description: Returns the index of the first occurrence in s of any character from chars, or std::string_view::npos if none. For UTF-8 characters, the index corresponds to the first byte of the sequence.
requirements: s and chars must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::EscapeString
functions.description: Escapes special HTML characters (<, >, &, ', ") in s to their entity forms. Guarantees UnescapeString(EscapeString(s)) == s.
requirements: s must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::Escape
functions.description: Writes the HTML-escaped form of s into the provided stringbuf. Escapes the five characters <, >, &, ', ".
requirements: escaped must be non-null and point to a valid std::stringbuf ready for writing.
s must remain valid during the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::UnescapeString
functions.signature: static void htmlparser::Strings::UnescapeString(std::string* s, bool attribute = false)
functions.description: In-place unescapes HTML entities in s (e.g., "a<b" -> "a<b"). If attribute is true, uses attribute-value parsing rules. It holds that UnescapeString(EscapeString(s)) == s, but not necessarily the converse.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::ToLower
functions.description: Converts all characters in s to lowercase in-place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::ToUpper
functions.description: Converts all characters in s to uppercase in-place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::IsAllWhitespaceChars
functions.signature: static bool htmlparser::Strings::IsAllWhitespaceChars(std::string_view s, std::string_view whitespace_chars = kWhitespace)
functions.description: Returns true if s consists only of characters from whitespace_chars (defaults to kWhitespace set).
requirements: s and whitespace_chars must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::EqualFold
functions.description: Case-insensitive string equality comparison.
requirements: l and r must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::Replace
functions.signature: static void htmlparser::Strings::Replace(std::string* s, std::string_view f, std::string_view t)
functions.description: Replaces the first occurrence of substring f in s with t, modifying s in place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.
Replacement is no-op if f is not found.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::ReplaceAll
functions.signature: static void htmlparser::Strings::ReplaceAll(std::string* s, std::string_view f, std::string_view t)
functions.description: Replaces all occurrences of substring f in s with t, modifying s in place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::ReplaceAny
functions.signature: static void htmlparser::Strings::ReplaceAny(std::string* s, std::string_view chars, std::string_view to)
functions.description: Replaces any occurrence in s of any character from chars with the string to, modifying s in place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::Translate
functions.signature: static std::optional<std::string> htmlparser::Strings::Translate(std::string_view str, std::string_view abc, std::string_view xyz)
functions.description: Translates characters in str by mapping each character in abc to the corresponding character in xyz. If abc has duplicates, earlier mappings take precedence. If abc is longer than xyz, unmatched characters in str are removed. Works with UTF-8; returns std::nullopt if any string contains UTF-8 that fails to decode.
requirements: str, abc, and xyz must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Callers must handle std::nullopt when UTF-8 decoding fails for any input string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::TrimLeft
functions.signature: static void htmlparser::Strings::TrimLeft(std::string* s, std::string_view chars_to_trim = kWhitespace)
functions.description: Removes leading characters in s that are present in chars_to_trim, in place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::TrimRight
functions.signature: static void htmlparser::Strings::TrimRight(std::string* s, std::string_view chars_to_trim = kWhitespace)
functions.description: Removes trailing characters in s that are present in chars_to_trim, in place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::Trim
functions.signature: static void htmlparser::Strings::Trim(std::string* s, std::string_view chars_to_trim = kWhitespace)
functions.description: Removes leading and trailing characters in s that are present in chars_to_trim, in place.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::StripTrailingNewline
functions.description: Removes a trailing newline from s if present, modifying the string. The meaning of the boolean return value is not documented in the header (likely indicates whether a newline was removed).
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::RemoveExtraSpaceChars
functions.description: Reduces all consecutive sequences of space characters to a single space, modifying s in place. The resulting string may shrink.
requirements: s must be non-null and point to a valid, mutable std::string.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::StartsWith
functions.description: Returns true if s starts with prefix.
requirements: s and prefix must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::EndsWith
functions.description: Returns true if s ends with suffix.
requirements: s and suffix must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::SplitStringAt
functions.description: Splits s on the given delimiter character and returns owned string columns.
requirements: s must remain valid only for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::SplitStrAtUtf8Whitespace
functions.description: Splits s on any UTF-8 or ASCII whitespace and returns views into the original string. The returned views alias s and are invalidated if s's storage is destroyed or modified.
requirements: The original string/buffer referenced by s must outlive all returned string_view elements.
s must remain unmodified while using the returned views.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::IsUtf8WhiteSpaceChar
functions.description: Determines whether the character at byte position in s is a whitespace character. Returns the number of bytes comprising that whitespace character (e.g., 3 for U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE). Returns 0 if the character at position is not whitespace.
requirements: position must be in the range [0, s.size()].
s must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::Strings::CountTerms
functions.description: Counts the number of terms in s, where terms are separated by whitespace and punctuation.
requirements: s must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::ProtocolStrict
functions.description: Extracts the URL scheme (protocol) per RFC 3986 §3.1. Returns an empty string_view if none found. Performs no normalization or validation beyond the protocol itself. The returned view refers to the input buffer.
requirements: url must remain valid for the duration of the call and as long as the returned string_view is used.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::URL
functions.description: Constructs a URL object and parses the provided URL. The URL stores the input as a std::string_view internally and parses components such as protocol, login, host, port, and path/params/fragment.
requirements: The character data referenced by url must outlive the URL instance, since the class stores a std::string_view to the original buffer.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::is_valid
functions.description: Indicates whether the parsed URL is valid according to the class’s parsing logic.
requirements: Call only on a constructed URL instance.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::has_protocol
functions.description: Returns true if the URL contains a protocol (scheme).
requirements: Call only on a constructed URL instance.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::protocol
functions.description: Returns the parsed protocol component as a std::string. No normalization is guaranteed by the header.
requirements: Call only on a constructed URL instance.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::hostname
functions.description: Returns the parsed hostname as a std::string.
requirements: Call only on a constructed URL instance.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::login
functions.description: Returns the parsed userinfo/login component as a std::string.
requirements: Call only on a constructed URL instance.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::port
functions.description: Returns the parsed port number. If no port is specified, the value depends on parsing defaults (not specified in header).
requirements: Call only on a constructed URL instance.

functions.name: htmlparser::URL::path_params_fragment
functions.description: Returns a view of the path, parameters, and fragment portion of the URL. The returned view aliases the original URL buffer stored by the object.
requirements: The returned string_view remains valid as long as the URL object (and its referenced underlying buffer) remains alive.

data_types.description: A string that may contain percent-escape sequences per URL encoding (e.g., %20, %2F, %3F). It can be a full URL or any URL component that uses percent-encoding. Non-encoded characters may appear alongside encoded bytes.
An unconstrained byte sequence treated as a generic string. It may contain any bytes including NULs, control characters, or invalid UTF-8.
A byte sequence intended to represent text encoded as UTF-8. May be valid or invalid; decoding routines should handle errors.
A string that may include HTML entity escapes such as <, >, &, ', " and possibly other entities, representing HTML or attribute text requiring unescaping.
A string composed only of letters and/or digits. In this context the fuzzer constructs ASCII letters for inputs to ensure valid UTF-8 and predictable translation behavior.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets functions that consume arbitrary byte strings, but many
# stubs exercise URL parsing and UTF-8/HTML string utilities. We therefore
# produce valid, interesting byte sequences that include:
# - Valid UTF-8 across 1–4 byte sequences
# - ASCII text with mixed case for ToLower/ToUpper/EqualFold
# - Whitespace variants including CR, LF, CRLF, tabs, form-feed, vertical tab
# - Repetitions of spaces for RemoveExtraSpaceChars
# - HTML escape-relevant characters: < > & ' "
# - Percent-encoded segments for DecodePercentEncodedURL and URL components
# - URL-like strings (with and without protocol, with login, ports, IPv6, query/fragment)
# - Strings containing delimiter candidates for SplitStringAt
# - Bytes including NUL (for kWhitespaceOrNull) and other control chars
# - Codepoint boundaries to exercise Utf8 decoding/encoding paths
#
# The output is a single bytes buffer; fuzz harness will slice it into different
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME inputs over time. We structure the buffer as a corpus
# of multiple lines/records separated by newlines and NULs so different slices
# are likely to pick diverse content.

ASCII_WHITESPACE = b" \t\r\n\f\v"
HTML_ESC = b"<>&\'\""
CONTROL_BYTES = bytes([0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x1F])

# Some valid multi-byte UTF-8 examples (2,3,4-byte sequences), including spaces.
UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "\u00A0",   # non-breaking space (2 bytes)
    "\u00E9",   # é
    "\u03B1",   # α
    "\u20AC",   # € (3 bytes)
    "\u2603",   # ☃
    "\u3000",   # IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE (UTF-8 3 bytes)
    "\U0001F600",  # 😀 (4 bytes)
    "\U0001F4A9",  # 💩
]

URL_TEMPLATES = [
    "http://example.com/",  # simple http
    "https://example.com/path?x=1&y=2#frag",
    "ftp://user:pass@host.example:21/path;param?query#frag",
    "mailto:user@example.com",
    "file:///C:/Windows/system32/drivers/etc/hosts",
    "//no-scheme.example.com/path",  # scheme-less
    "custom+ext-proto://host/path",
    "http://[2001:db8::1]/index.html",
    "http://example.com/%7Euser/%E2%82%AC",  # percent enc + UTF8
    "ws://example.com/socket?token=abc%20123",
]

PERCENT_ENCODED_PARTS = [
    b"simple%20space%2Fslash%3Fq%3D1",
    b"mixed%25percent%2Bplus%26amp",
    b"utf8-%E2%82%AC-%F0%9F%98%80",
]

DELIMS = [ord(','), ord('|'), ord(':'), ord(';'), ord('\t')]


def _rand_weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List, weights: List[int]):
    total = sum(weights)
    x = rng.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if x < acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]


def _rand_utf8_chunk(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a chunk containing a mix of ASCII words, UTF-8 samples, and digits.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Random ASCII word with mixed case
    word_len = rng.randint(1, 16)
    word = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(word_len))
    parts.append(word.encode('ascii'))
    # Optional UTF-8 code points
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        cp = rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES)
        parts.append(cp.encode('utf-8'))
    # Include some HTML escape chars
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        k = rng.randint(1, 4)
        parts.append(bytes(rng.choices(list(HTML_ESC), k=k)))
    # Include whitespace run
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        parts.append(b" ")
        parts.append(b"   ")
    return b"".join(parts)


def _rand_newline_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create text with different newline styles to exercise ConvertNewLines and StripTrailingNewline.
    lines = []
    num = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for i in range(num):
        body = _rand_utf8_chunk(rng)
        nl = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, [b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\r"], [5, 3, 2])
        lines.append(body + nl)
    return b"".join(lines)


def _rand_url(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base = rng.choice(URL_TEMPLATES).encode('utf-8')
    # Optionally append extra path/query params and escapes
    tail = b""
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        tail += b"path-" + _rand_utf8_chunk(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        tail += b"?q=" + rng.choice(PERCENT_ENCODED_PARTS)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tail += b"#frag-" + _rand_utf8_chunk(rng)
    return base + tail


def _rand_split_candidate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build CSV/TSV-like content with various delimiters.
    delim = rng.choice(DELIMS)
    cols = [
        _rand_utf8_chunk(rng),
        b"value123",
        b"A<B>&\"'C",  # includes escapables
        b"  spaced   out  ",
    ]
    row = bytes([delim]).join(cols)
    # multiple rows
    rows = [row]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        mutated = bytearray(row)
        # insert NUL or control occasionally
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pos = rng.randrange(1, len(mutated))
            mutated.insert(pos, 0)
        rows.append(bytes(mutated))
    return b"\n".join(rows)


def _section(rng: random.Random, title: str, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Frame sections with markers that are benign strings; harness may pick substrings.
    return (b"--BEGIN-" + title.encode('ascii') + b"--\n" + payload + b"\n--END-" + title.encode('ascii') + b"--\n")


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Mixed ASCII/UTF-8 with HTML escapables and whitespace runs
    for i in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        sections.append(_section(rng, f"UTF8-{i}", _rand_utf8_chunk(rng)))

    # 2) Newline variants block
    sections.append(_section(rng, "NEWLINES", _rand_newline_block(rng)))

    # 3) URL cases (with and without schemes), including percent-encoding
    for i in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        sections.append(_section(rng, f"URL-{i}", _rand_url(rng)))

    # 4) Pure percent-encoded strings to feed DecodePercentEncodedURL
    pe = b"\n".join(PERCENT_ENCODED_PARTS + [b"a%20b%2Fc%3Fd%3D1%26e%3D2%25"])
    sections.append(_section(rng, "PERCENT", pe))

    # 5) Split delimiter candidate data
    sections.append(_section(rng, "SPLIT", _rand_split_candidate(rng)))

    # 6) Whitespace-only strings to test IsAllWhitespaceChars (with and w/o NUL)
    ws_only = bytearray()
    for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 20)):
        ws_only.append(rng.choice(list(ASCII_WHITESPACE)))
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        ws_only.append(0x00)
    sections.append(_section(rng, "WHITESPACE", bytes(ws_only)))

    # 7) Include some control bytes and boundary values for ASCII checks
    ascii_checks = bytearray()
    ascii_checks += b"AZaz09!"  # boundaries for IsCharAlphabet/IsDigit
    ascii_checks += CONTROL_BYTES
    ascii_checks += b"\x7F"  # DEL
    sections.append(_section(rng, "ASCII", bytes(ascii_checks)))

    # 8) Trailing newline exercise strings
    sections.append(_section(rng, "TRAIL-NL", b"line1\nline2\r\nend\n"))

    # 9) Add a long run with many spaces to test RemoveExtraSpaceChars
    sections.append(_section(rng, "SPACES", b"word" + b" " * rng.randint(5, 20) + b"end"))

    # 10) Add some exact tokens for Replace/ReplaceAll/ReplaceAny testing
    sections.append(_section(rng, "REPLACE", b"foo bar foo <tag> & entity ' \" "))

    blob = b"".join(sections)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]

    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for HTML-with-entities content that remains valid after unescaping
# and re-escaping round trips used by the fuzzer stub:
#   original -> EscapeString -> UnescapeString(attribute|!attribute) == original
# We therefore need to generate arbitrary original text (not necessarily valid HTML)
# consisting of a wide range of characters, including ones that trigger escaping
# (<, >, &, ', "), whitespace/newlines, Unicode, and edge cases like lone semicolons
# or ampersands that should be preserved through Escape/Unescape cycle.
# The stub will use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain this buffer.
# No filenames are used in this stub.

HTML_BASIC_ENTITIES = ["<", ">", "&", "'", """]

def _rand_ascii(rnd: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix visible ASCII and whitespace; include characters that do not get escaped
    # to increase coverage of general string processing.
    alphabet = (
        string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    )
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rnd.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_unicode_block(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a small sequence of valid UTF-8 characters from diverse ranges.
    # Avoid surrogate range and invalid code points.
    out: List[str] = []
    choices = []
    # Basic Latin extended punctuation
    choices += list(range(0x00A1, 0x00FF))
    # Latin Extended-A subset
    choices += list(range(0x0100, 0x017F))
    # Greek subset
    choices += list(range(0x0370, 0x03A2))
    # Cyrillic subset
    choices += list(range(0x0400, 0x045F))
    # Emoji subset (common ones)
    choices += [0x2600, 0x2601, 0x2602, 0x2615, 0x263A, 0x2665, 0x2728]
    # Some CJK characters
    choices += [0x4E00, 0x4E2D, 0x56FD, 0x65E5, 0x672C, 0x6C49, 0x8A9E]
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 12)):
        cp = rnd.choice(choices)
        try:
            out.append(chr(cp))
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return "".join(out)

def _insert_entities(rnd: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Insert pre-escaped entities that should remain stable through the cycle.
    parts = [s]
    # Randomly interleave known entities and numeric entities
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 6)):
        idx = rnd.randint(0, len(parts))
        ent_kind = rnd.randint(0, 3)
        if ent_kind == 0:
            ent = rnd.choice(HTML_BASIC_ENTITIES)
        elif ent_kind == 1:
            # Decimal numeric entity for a printable character
            cp = rnd.choice([34, 38, 39, 60, 62, 160, 169, 174, 215, 247])
            ent = f"&#{cp};"
        else:
            # Hex numeric entity
            cp = rnd.choice([0x22, 0x26, 0x27, 0x3C, 0x3E, 0xA0, 0x2022, 0x2014])
            ent = f"&#x{cp:X};"
        parts.insert(idx, ent)
    return "".join(parts)

def _structured_htmlish(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create small HTML-like snippets to ensure escaping of tag syntax.
    tags = [
        ("div", {"class": "c&c", "data-x": "1<2"}),
        ("a", {"href": "https://example.com/?q=1&x=2", "title": "A\"B"}),
        ("span", {"data-v": "'quote' & more"}),
        ("p", {}),
    ]
    name, attrs = rnd.choice(tags)
    attr_parts = []
    for k, v in attrs.items():
        q = rnd.choice(['"', "'"])
        attr_parts.append(f"{k}={q}{v}{q}")
    attr_str = (" " + " ".join(attr_parts)) if attr_parts else ""
    inner = _rand_ascii(rnd, 0, 24) + _rand_unicode_block(rnd)
    # Sprinkle raw special chars in inner
    specials = ['<', '>', '&', '\'', '"']
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 5)):
        pos = rnd.randint(0, len(inner))
        inner = inner[:pos] + rnd.choice(specials) + inner[pos:]
    return f"<{name}{attr_str}>{inner}</{name}>"

def _mix_newlines_and_space(rnd: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Introduce various newline styles and whitespace runs which should be
    # preserved by Escape/Unescape.
    nl_variants = ["\n", "\r", "\r\n", "\f", "\t", " "]
    chunks = [s]
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 6)):
        chunks.insert(rnd.randint(0, len(chunks)), rnd.choice(nl_variants) * rnd.randint(1, 3))
    return "".join(chunks)

def _build_original(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    pieces: List[str] = []
    # Start with structured htmlish content to ensure presence of escapables
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        pieces.append(_structured_htmlish(rnd))
    # Add random ascii and unicode blocks
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        block = _rand_ascii(rnd, 5, 40)
        if rnd.random() < 0.6:
            block = _insert_entities(rnd, block)
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            block += _rand_unicode_block(rnd)
        pieces.append(block)
    s = " ".join(pieces)
    s = _mix_newlines_and_space(rnd, s)

    # Edge-case prefixes/suffixes: leading/trailing spaces, tabs, and semicolons
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        s = (" " * rnd.randint(0, 3)) + s
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        s = s + ("\t" * rnd.randint(0, 3))

    # Include stray ampersands and incomplete entities that should be preserved
    # (they will be escaped first and then unescaped back to original text).
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        insert_positions = [rnd.randint(0, len(s)) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3))]
        for pos in sorted(insert_positions):
            s = s[:pos] + rnd.choice(["&x", "&", "¬anentity;", "&&", "&;", "&#", "&#x"]) + s[pos:]

    # Cap size to 4096 bytes
    if len(s.encode('utf-8')) > 4096:
        # Truncate at code-point boundary by encoding and slicing
        b = s.encode('utf-8')[:4096]
        # Ensure valid UTF-8 by backing up to a safe boundary
        while b and (b[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            b = b[:-1]
        try:
            s = b.decode('utf-8', 'strict')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            s = b.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    original = _build_original(rnd)
    return original.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets htmlparser::Strings::Translate fuzzer stub.
# The stub builds its own ASCII-only strings from FUZZ_PARAM_STR bytes by mapping
# each byte to 'a' + (c % 26) for str and abc (with abc deduplicated) and builds xyz
# either as identity (xyz == abc) or as an uppercase mapping of equal length.
# We therefore provide a buffer that, when split by the harness into FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# calls, yields diverse but valid ASCII inputs that exercise:
# - identity mapping (ensures equality)
# - non-identity mapping with same-length xyz
# - abc containing duplicates, gaps, and full alphabet coverage
# We avoid invalid UTF-8 entirely and keep under 4096 bytes.

# Assumed harness consumption order within this stub:
#   raw         = FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
#   abc_raw     = FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
#   identity flag is random in harness (not from buffer), but we craft data to be
#                interesting for both branches.
#   xyz_raw     = FUZZ_PARAM_STR()  (only used if identity == false)
# Many fuzzers concatenate all provided seed buffers and split them per FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# based on delimiters or sizes. We encode three segments with length headers so that
# common corpus loaders can split deterministically.

# Encoding format we use for our bytes buffer:
# [len1(2 bytes LE)] raw_bytes
# [len2(2 bytes LE)] abc_raw_bytes
# [len3(2 bytes LE)] xyz_raw_bytes
# All bytes are ASCII and constrained so that the stub’s mapping yields desired coverage.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_SEG = 1200


def _pack_len(n: int) -> bytes:
    return n.to_bytes(2, 'little')


def _make_raw(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # raw -> becomes str: 'a' + (c % 26). We want words, spaces are ignored by mapping
    # so just create varied sequences that after mapping give patterns to translate.
    # Include all letters by ensuring c % 26 covers 0..25 multiple times.
    length = rng.randint(64, 512)
    # Build with values 0..255 but ensure spread across mod 26.
    out = bytearray()
    base_cycle = [i for i in range(26)]
    rng.shuffle(base_cycle)
    while len(out) < length:
        for v in base_cycle:
            out.append((v + rng.randrange(0, 230)) & 0xFF)
            if len(out) >= length:
                break
    return bytes(out)


def _make_abc_raw(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # abc is deduplicated after mapping to 'a'+(c%26). We want:
    # - sometimes small abc (e.g., 3 chars)
    # - sometimes full alphabet
    # - duplicates in source to test dedup logic
    mode = rng.randrange(4)
    if mode == 0:
        # small abc around 3-6 unique letters with many duplicates
        target_uniques = rng.randint(3, 6)
    elif mode == 1:
        # medium 10-15 uniques
        target_uniques = rng.randint(10, 15)
    elif mode == 2:
        # full alphabet
        target_uniques = 26
    else:
        # single-letter mapping
        target_uniques = 1

    # Create values that map to chosen unique set.
    letters = list(range(26))
    rng.shuffle(letters)
    chosen = letters[:target_uniques]

    # Populate with duplicates and noise that maps into chosen set.
    size = rng.randint(max(8, target_uniques * 2), min(MAX_SEG, target_uniques * 20))
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < size:
        v = rng.choice(chosen)
        # Add random higher byte to vary original value while keeping mod 26 == v
        k = rng.randrange(0, 10)
        val = (v + 26 * k) & 0xFF
        out.append(val)
        # inject occasional bytes that map to same chosen via different residue
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            k2 = rng.randrange(10, 20)
            out.append((v + 26 * k2) & 0xFF)
    return bytes(out)


def _make_xyz_raw(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # xyz_raw is only used to build uppercase mapping: for i in abc.size(), pick
    # c from xyz_raw or from i. Only c % 26 matters. To vary, craft a buffer that,
    # when mod 26 applied across positions, yields a shuffled A..Z coverage.
    # We'll emit a random permutation of 0..25 twice.
    perms: List[int] = list(range(26))
    rng.shuffle(perms)
    seq = perms + perms  # ensure enough bytes for long abc
    # Map residues to bytes: just use the residue itself to keep simple.
    data = bytes((v for v in seq))
    # Pad a bit randomly
    pad_len = rng.randint(0, 64)
    pad = bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(pad_len))
    return data + pad


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    raw = _make_raw(rng)
    abc_raw = _make_abc_raw(rng)
    xyz_raw = _make_xyz_raw(rng)

    # Ensure total size within limit
    parts = [_pack_len(len(raw)), raw, _pack_len(len(abc_raw)), abc_raw,
             _pack_len(len(xyz_raw)), xyz_raw]
    buf = b''.join(parts)
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Trim xyz_raw first, then others if necessary
        # Rebuild with trimmed xyz
        avail = MAX_TOTAL - (2 + len(raw) + 2 + len(abc_raw))
        if avail < 2:
            # extreme fallback: trim all proportionally
            raw = raw[:min(len(raw), 1024)]
            abc_raw = abc_raw[:min(len(abc_raw), 1024)]
            xyz_raw = xyz_raw[:min(len(xyz_raw), 1024)]
        else:
            xyz_raw = xyz_raw[:max(0, avail - 2)]
        parts = [_pack_len(len(raw)), raw, _pack_len(len(abc_raw)), abc_raw,
                 _pack_len(len(xyz_raw)), xyz_raw]
        buf = b''.join(parts)

    return buf
